title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
events_chronological: In 1966 Harriet Vanger disappears from Hedeby Island during a parade, on a day when a crash has blocked the only bridge.
Every year since, Henrik Vanger has received a pressed flower on his birthday, which he takes as taunting from her killer.
Journalist Mikael Blomkvist loses a libel case against the financier Hans-Erik Wennerstrom and resigns from Millennium.
Lisbeth Salander, a ward of the state and a researcher for Milton Security, is handed a new guardian, Nils Bjurman, after her old one has a stroke.
Salander compiles the background report on Blomkvist that persuades Henrik Vanger to hire him.
Henrik brings Blomkvist to Hedeby to write a family history and, in truth, to find out who killed Harriet.
Bjurman makes Salander perform oral sex before he will release her own money.
Bjurman rapes Salander at his flat, not knowing she has hidden a camera in her bag.
Salander comes back, tasers Bjurman, tattoos him as a rapist and blackmails him with the recording.
Blomkvist works through the Vanger archive, is shot at in the woods, and finds Harriet's notebook full of names and numbers.
Blomkvist's daughter Pernilla points out that the numbers are Bible verses.
Blomkvist asks Milton Security for a research assistant and is given Salander, who has been reading his hard drive for months.
Together they match the verses to a series of ritual murders of women across Sweden going back to the 1940s.
They trace the killings to Gottfried Vanger, Harriet's father, and then to her brother Martin.
Martin catches Blomkvist, chains him in a soundproofed basement and explains what he does down there.
Salander arrives, splits Martin's face with a golf club, and lets him drive away to his death in a crash.
Salander nurses Blomkvist back to health and the two become lovers.
Anita Vanger in London turns out to be Harriet herself, living under her cousin's name since fleeing her father and brother.
Harriet comes home to Henrik, and Blomkvist has his story.
Salander, in disguise, empties Wennerstrom's accounts in Zurich and feeds Blomkvist the story that destroys him, then sees him with Erika and throws away the present she had bought.
syuzhet_notes: The film runs two threads in parallel for its first half - Blomkvist on Hedeby Island and Salander in Stockholm - cutting between them long before they have anything to do with each other, and converging them at told-order bullet 12. Told-order bullets 4-5 are the 1966 disappearance and the years of pressed flowers, reconstructed from photographs and Henrik's account rather than played as present action.
fabula_notes: Harriet's disappearance and the ritual murders reaching back to the 1940s are pieced together from documents and photographs and never dramatised as they happened, so the ordering of those events is what the investigation establishes rather than what the film shows. Salander's own history, alluded to only as "all the evil", stays off screen in this film.
